title: Hang a hooked strainer across a bowl: hook on the right rim, handle on the left
instruction: Hang the fine-mesh strainer across the bowl: its hook over the right rim and its handle on the left rim, the mesh hanging in the bowl clear of the stock. Then let go.
context: Resting a hooked fine-mesh strainer across a bowl is a familiar home-kitchen skill: people do it to strain stock, pasta water, custard or a jelly base, or to let a rinsed strainer drain. The hook is set over one rim and the handle rests on the opposite rim, so the strainer cannot slide or tip into the bowl while the person turns to the pot. The mesh must hang clear of what is already in the bowl: a mesh sitting in the strained liquid clogs and the next pour backs up and runs over. Set on the rims without the hook engaged, the strainer can slide off. A robot that helps in a kitchen has to hang it this way and let go without nudging the bowl or the strainer.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. A counter scene of six objects. (1) A silicone non-slip mat, 260 x 260 x 4 mm, grey-blue, lying centred at x 300 mm, y 0 (friction est 0.9). (2) A stainless mixing bowl, 0.30 kg: 220 mm across its rolled rim bead (8 mm), 200 mm across inside the rim, 105 mm tall, its wall flaring from 140 mm inside at the floor, standing loose on the mat centred at x 300 mm, y 0. It holds 0.5 L of strained stock (0.52 kg, amber), 30 mm deep, so the stock's top is 32 mm above the bowl's foot; the rim's top is 105 mm above it. (3) A fine-mesh strainer, stainless, 0.12 kg (est), lying mesh down on the table, its long axis along y, handle toward +y (the left arm), its ring centred at x 300 mm, y +252 mm: a ring 130 mm across and 57 mm tall with a 0.5 mm mesh floor; a folded handle 18 mm wide with 10 mm flanges, from the ring out to 192.5 mm from its centre; and opposite it a bowl-rest hook, a strap 18 mm wide bent over, its legs 30 mm apart (outer leg 20 mm, inner leg 12 mm long), its outside 121.5 mm from the ring's centre. The strainer is 314 mm long. Hung across the bowl with the hook over the right (-y) rim and the handle on the left (+y) rim, the ring hangs inside with its mesh 58 mm above the bowl's foot, 26 mm above the stock. It is picked up by the handle next to the ring (gripper opening 94 mm). Real match: a widely sold stainless 5 in (13 cm) fine-mesh kitchen strainer with a bent-over bowl-rest hook opposite its handle, such as the kind sold as a 5 in bowl-rest or hook strainer. Acceptance check with a ruler and calipers; only a strainer within all ranges is used: ring 125-135 mm across and 52-62 mm tall; handle 16-20 mm wide, ring centre to its end 187-198 mm; hook legs 28-32 mm apart, outer leg 17-23 mm and inner leg 10-14 mm long; overall length 305-325 mm; mass 100-200 g. An inexpensive kitchenware-store item (typically under 15 USD). Not a miniature (under 8 cm) strainer. (4) A stainless stock pot, 190 mm across, 200 mm tall, fixed, centred at x 420 mm, y -300 mm. (5) A tiled backsplash wall, 20 mm thick, 900 mm wide, 300 mm tall, fixed, its front face at x 565 mm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the strainer, the bowl and both grippers; distances are taken in the bowl's own frame (its axis through the centre of its floor; the rim's bead centre line at 105 mm radius). Hook on: the hook's inner leg face is 100 mm or less from the bowl's axis and its outer leg face 110 mm or more (top view), so the bead lies in the hook's gap, the strap's underside is within 6 mm above the bead's top and no more than 2 mm below it, and the hook's middle is within 45 degrees of straight right (-y) of the bowl's axis (top view). Handle on: where the handle's underside crosses the far bead (within 5 mm of its centre line) it is within 6 mm above the bead's top and no more than 2 mm below it. Ring in: the ring's centre within 30 mm of the bowl's axis (top view). Mesh clear: the mesh's underside is 15 mm or more above the stock's top (47 mm or more above the bowl's foot) and at least 20 mm below the rim's top. Level: the long axis within 10 degrees of horizontal, the strainer within 15 degrees of upright, and the long axis passing within 20 mm of the bowl's axis (any direction across the round bowl counts). Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the strainer and the bowl, and over that 1 s the strainer and the bowl each move under 5 mm and turn under 5 degrees (no visible motion). Score 0 if at any time either part's lowest point is more than 20 mm below the table top, 0 unless hands off, and 0 unless the bowl ends in place: at the last step its foot is within 30 mm of its mark (top view), not lifted 20 mm and tipped no more than 10 degrees. The bowl may be pushed or knocked on the way and put right: only where it ends counts. Otherwise: 1.0 hook on, handle on, ring in, mesh clear and level; 0.5 ring in and mesh clear with the long axis within 25 degrees of horizontal (it rests across the rims, not hooked, hooked off line or on another part of the rim); 0 otherwise (on the table, on the pot, or the mesh down in the stock, where it clogs). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: hook on, 100 mm and 110 mm radius templates on the rim, a 6 mm feeler that must not pass under the strap and a 45 degree set square from the bowl's centre; handle on, a 6 mm feeler that must not pass under the handle; ring in, a 30 mm radius circle drawn about the bowl's axis; mesh clear, the bowl is empty and dry (no water, so no spill risk) and a rule inside it is read against marks 32 (the simulated stock's top), 47 and 85 mm above its foot; level, a 10 and a 15 degree protractor and a rule across the bowl; hands off, 30 mm spacer blocks and 30 fps video of the last 1 s against a taped mark on the table at the strainer's handle and the bowl's foot, in which neither shows visible motion; bowl's final place, a taped outline 30 mm outside its foot and a 10 degree protractor; fall, a rule on the table.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The mesh is a 2 mm solid floor; the ring, hook and folded handle are boxes. The bowl's flared wall is 24 flat slabs with the rolled bead as 24 boxes; the stock is a solid disc (no sloshing, no clogging). Friction: steel on steel 0.4, silicone mat 0.9 (est). The pot and wall are fixed. Strainer sizes follow a typical 5 in strainer; bowl and mass figures are estimates, to be measured in a real trial.
reset_notes: Lay the mat and set the bowl centred on it (x 300 mm, y 0) empty and dry for a real trial (no water, no spill risk): tape a mark 32 mm above its foot for the simulated stock's top (the sim bowl holds 0.5 L of stock, 30 mm deep). Lay the strainer mesh down on the table, its ring centred at x 300 mm, y +252 mm, handle toward +y along y, hook toward the bowl. Set the pot and the wall in place. Dry the strainer and the rim. Nothing is consumed.
